transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Well, they say I’m here because I used up our savings. I spent it on wood, lights, and all this display stuff. I just kept pushing the work, you know, working way after dark. But... I really felt like if I stopped, the whole house and the whole block would just lose its chance. So, that's why they brought me in.
During the time you were working late and spending money on the display, did you feel unusually upbeat, irritable, or like you didn’t need as much sleep as usual?

Yeah, I'd say both. Most days I just feel... well, really charged up. Almost joyful, honestly. It feels like I'm young again, getting all this done. But then, if my wife starts questioning what I'm doing, or if the contractors push back on me, I get hot fast. I just lose my temper and start yelling.
Did you find yourself working intensely on projects, feeling driven to keep going, or having so much energy that you couldn’t sit still during this time?

Yes, exactly. I just couldn't stop moving. I mean, I can't just sit in my chair anymore. I'm always up, going from the garden to the darkroom, out to the porch... just carrying my tools around, fixing things before anyone even asks me to. I just have to keep going.
Would you say that this feeling of being charged up and joyful was a change from how you usually feel, or is this more like your normal self? Did it seem out of character for you?

I'm not really sure. I mean... my wife keeps saying it's not like me, but to me, it just feels like me. I haven't really thought about it being out of character or anything like that. 

I just feel good, you know? Better than I have in a long time. So... I don't know if I'd call it a change, exactly. It's just me finally having the energy to get done what needs doing.

Would you say there was a specific time when your mood was consistently higher or more intense than it usually is — something that you or others around you could clearly notice as different from your typical self?

Well, like I was saying before, it's mostly been this feeling of just being really charged up. My wife definitely noticed it. I feel joyful, honestly, like I have the energy I had when I was a younger man. But yeah, it's not always just a good mood. If she starts asking too many questions about what I'm doing, or if the guys working on the house don't do what I say, I get hot fast. I just lose my temper and start yelling at them. So I guess that intensity is what people are noticing.
Would you say that this period of feeling charged up and joyful was clearly different from how you normally feel, or has it been more like your usual mood all along?

Well, like I was just saying a minute ago... to me, it feels like my usual self. Just, you know, with a lot more pep. I don't really sit around thinking about if I'm acting different. I just wake up and feel good. It's my wife who keeps telling me I'm not acting like my normal self. So... I guess if you ask her, it's clearly different. But to me, I'm just being me.
Would you say that this period of feeling charged up and irritable was a distinct change from how you usually are, even if it felt natural to you at the time?

Well, like I said... to me, it just feels like I'm finally myself again. I wake up most days feeling really charged up, almost joyful, you know? Like I'm a young man again with all this energy. But... I guess the irritability part is a change. If my wife starts questioning me, or if those contractors don't listen to how I want things done, I do get hot real fast. I just start yelling. I don't usually fly off the handle like that. So, yeah, I suppose that part is different from how I normally am.
How long have you been feeling this way — this period of feeling charged up, joyful, and irritable?

It's been about three months now. I'd say it all started right around the time the remodeling began. Everything in the house got turned upside down, and that's when this whole feeling really kicked in.

Have you had any period where your mood was not just better than usual, but clearly and consistently elevated, expansive, or irritable — to the point that other people noticed and it was a real change from your usual self?

Yeah, that's pretty much what I've been trying to tell you. This whole time right now is exactly like that. Most days I just feel really charged up and almost joyful, like I'm a young man again with all this energy. But like I mentioned before, if my wife starts in on me, or those contractors question how I want things done, I get hot fast and just start yelling. My wife definitely notices it. She's the one who keeps saying it's a real big change from how I usually am.

Would you say that during this time, your mood was not just better than usual, but clearly and consistently different from how you normally feel — like a switch that turned on, making you act in a way that others around you could clearly notice as different?

Well, I feel like I kind of just answered that, but... yes. Exactly. It's not just me having a regular good day. It's... well, I guess you could say it's like a switch got flipped, yeah. 

Like I was just saying, my wife definitely notices it. She's the one telling me I'm acting completely different from how I normally am. So, yes, it's a clear change.

Have you had a period lasting at least a week where you felt constantly 'charged up' or unusually irritable, along with a noticeable increase in activity — like working on projects nonstop — that was clearly different from your usual behavior when you're not depressed?

Yeah, definitely. It's been going on way longer than a week, like I said. And the activity part... yeah. I can't just sit in my chair anymore. I'm constantly up and moving around. I go from the garden, then down to the darkroom, out to the porch... just carrying tools around and fixing things before anybody even asks me to. I just can't seem to stop moving.

During this time when you felt so charged up and were working on all these projects, did you find that you needed less sleep than usual — like you could stay up late and still feel rested with just a few hours of sleep?

No, not really. I mean, I'm sleeping about the same as I always do. I might be up early sometimes because I've got so much on my mind, but I wouldn't say I need less sleep. I still get my regular hours in, mostly. I haven't noticed any big change with my sleeping, just the energy during the day.

During this time when you felt so charged up and were working so intensely, did you find yourself thinking faster than usual, getting distracted easily, or feeling like you had special abilities or powers?

Well, I wouldn't say I have any special powers or anything like that. But my mind... yeah, I guess it's moving pretty fast. And getting distracted? Definitely. I'll be out there measuring a wall for a project, and then... I don't know, I'll hear a bird, or someone hammering down the street, or just a car driving by, and it just pulls my attention right off what I'm doing. Before I even realize it, I've walked away and started on some completely different job. It's hard to just stick to one thing right now.
Would you say that this period when you felt so charged up, irritable, and constantly active has lasted for at least one full week?

Well, yeah... like I mentioned a few minutes ago, it's definitely been going on for more than just a week. It's been a while now that I've been feeling this way, just constantly having to move around.

Have you noticed any of the following during this time: feeling like you're invincible or have special abilities, talking more than usual, racing thoughts, or getting involved in risky activities that could have serious consequences?

Well, like I said a minute ago, I don't have any special powers or anything like that. And I'm not doing anything dangerous. But the talking... yeah, I guess I am talking a whole lot more. 

Once I start explaining my plans to get all these projects done, the words just keep coming. My wife actually gets pretty frustrated with me. She says I run right over her before she can even get a single sentence in. I don't mean to, it's just... I have all these things to say and they just come pouring out.
